### T-01 - Stolen vendor credentials used on VPN

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| STRIDE | Spoofing |
| Assets | A-09 Remote-access gateway (SSL VPN), A-22 Vendor remote support (RoboServ) |
| Data flows | DF-09 |
| Threat | An attacker who phishes or buys RoboServ credentials logs in to the SSL VPN as the shared 'roboserv' account and is indistinguishable from the vendor. |
| Threat actor | TA-2 Initial access broker, TA-1 Cybercriminal / ransomware affiliate |
| Attack path | Vendor phishing / credential marketplace -> SSL VPN -> jump server |
| Existing controls | Password-only VPN; single shared vendor account; account always enabled |
| Likelihood x Impact | 4 x 5 = **20 Critical** |
| Recommended mitigation | SC-01 Secure vendor remote access; SC-04 Privileged access management & least privilege; SC-16 Supplier security requirements |
| Residual | 2 x 5 = **10 High** |
| Attack scenarios | AS-01 |

### T-02 - Unauthorized PLC logic modification

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| STRIDE | Tampering |
| Assets | A-11 Engineering workstation (EWS), A-14 PLC-01 Conveyor, A-15 PLC-02 Robotic welding cell, A-16 PLC-03 Packaging |
| Data flows | DF-03 |
| Threat | Any host that reaches a PLC on its engineering port can download modified logic, because PLCs are in REMOTE mode and the protocol has no authentication. |

| Attack path | Compromised EWS or any OT host -> engineering protocol -> PLC |
| Existing controls | Vendor engineering software requires a project password (offline only) |
| Likelihood x Impact | 3 x 5 = **15 High** |
| Recommended mitigation | SC-07 PLC change management & integrity; SC-03 Control-zone conduit and switch hardening; SC-10 OT network monitoring (passive IDS) |
| Residual | 1 x 5 = **5 Medium** |
| Attack scenarios | AS-01, AS-03 |
